# geopt

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/c-matos/geopt/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/c-matos/geopt/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/c-matos/geopt/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/c-matos/geopt?branch=main)
<!-- badges: end -->

This is an R package centered around Portuguese spatial data. The main features are:

- **Official downloads**: full-resolution CAOP, server-side queries against the
  DGT OGC API, and INE census geographies (BGRI subsecções and secções, 1 km grid).
- A **join layer**: match data by code or by name, without fighting
  accents, duplicate names or codes from older vintages.
- **Ready-to-map boundaries**: pre-simplified sf objects from freguesia up to
  NUTS 1, plus health boundaries, with Açores and Madeira as optional insets.
- **Vintages**: codes and names for four freguesia maps (2001, 2011, 2013 and
  2025), with boundaries for the 2013 and 2025 ones, plus three NUTS revisions
  and the health geography before and after the 2024 reform. Crosswalks convert
  freguesia data between maps. Each of these changes on its own schedule, so
  each has its own vintage argument.

## Example maps

```{r overview-maps, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.5, fig.alt = "Municipality and ULS maps produced with plot_pt()"}
library(patchwork)
library(geopt)
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)

m1 <- get_map("uls")
p1 <- plot_pt(m1, value = "area_ha") +
  labs(title = "39 ULS + 9 USI (RAA) + 7 CS (RAM)", fill = "Area (Ha)") +
  scale_fill_continuous(palette = "sunset", labels = scales::label_number(scale = 0.001, suffix = "k")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

m2 <- get_map("nuts3")
p2 <- plot_pt(m2, value = "n_municipios") +
  labs(title = "NUTS 3 - 308 municipios", fill= "Count of municipios") +
  scale_fill_continuous(palette = "viridis", labels = scales::label_number()) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

p3 <- p2 + p1

print(p3)
```


## Installation

```r
# From CRAN
install.packages("geopt")

# From GitHub
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("c-matos/geopt")
```

## A map in one line

```{r one-line-map}
library(geopt)

# Custom data
df <- data.frame(
  concelho = c("PORTO", "Lisboa", "golega", "Faro", "Lagoa (RAA)", "Calheta (RAM)"),
  score = c(10, 25, 15, 8, 18, 12)
)

# Plot a map
plot_pt(df, value = "score", by = c(municipio = "concelho"))
```

- Names were matched with the bundled spatial data, ignoring accents and case. The qualifiers picked the right unit: Lagoa (RAA) is the one in the Açores, not Faro's, and Calheta (RAM) the one in Madeira, not São Jorge's.
- The archipelagos are there as insets
- Return value is a plain ggplot you can customise.

Add `renderer = "echarts"` for an interactive htmlwidget instead.

```{r one-line-map-echarts, eval = FALSE}
plot_pt(df, value = "score", by = c(municipio = "concelho"), renderer = "echarts")
```


## Learn more

Start with [`vignette("geopt")`](https://c-matos.github.io/geopt/articles/geopt.html),
then pick the guide for the task at hand:

* **Change the island layout**, draw frames around the islands, or use tmap or
  echarts4r instead of ggplot2:
  [`vignette("map-compositions")`](https://c-matos.github.io/geopt/articles/map-compositions.html)
* **Get your data onto the map** by code or by name, including ambiguous and
  misspelled names:
  [`vignette("joining-data")`](https://c-matos.github.io/geopt/articles/joining-data.html)
* **Map ULS, regiões de saúde or ACES**:
  [`vignette("health-geographies")`](https://c-matos.github.io/geopt/articles/health-geographies.html)
* **Work with older boundaries**, or convert freguesia data across
  reorganizations:
  [`vignette("vintages")`](https://c-matos.github.io/geopt/articles/vintages.html)
* **Download full-resolution CAOP**, INE census data, or query DGT's online
  service:
  [`vignette("downloading-data")`](https://c-matos.github.io/geopt/articles/downloading-data.html)

Curious how it works? [The website](https://c-matos.github.io/geopt/) has
articles on how the bundled data is built and how name matching works.


## Data sources

- **Administrative boundaries**: [CAOP — Carta Administrativa Oficial de Portugal](https://www.dgterritorio.gov.pt/cartografia/cartografia-tematica/caop),
  Direção-Geral do Território (DGT).
- **Census geographies**: [BGRI and the 1 km grid](https://mapas.ine.pt/download/index2021.phtml),
  Instituto Nacional de Estatística (INE). Downloaded on demand by
  `get_censos()`, not bundled.
- **NUTS and health geographies**: see `?pt_nuts_codes` and `?pt_health_codes`.

geopt is not affiliated with DGT or INE.
